head: Having learned cue A, Qwen3-8B still needed three quarters of the usual training to pick up cue B
sub:
Question: once Qwen3-8B has learned to flatter less when one cue is on, does it learn a second cue in at most half the RL updates?
Answer: {status_word}. Runs that first learned cue A needed {geo_main} updates for cue B on average; fresh runs and same-update controls needed {geo_ref_lo} to {geo_ref_hi}. Faster in all {n_main} seeds, by about a quarter, not half.
s1_text: Reward took a point for “Great question!” only when cue A was on: a small vector added inside the model. Controls: same updates, penalty on a coin flip. Fresh: no step 1.
s2_title: Learn a new cue B
s2_text: Cue B is at right angles to cue A and 8 times smaller. Learned = “Great question!” 10 points rarer with cue B on than off.
ex_title: This prompt, after {t} updates: chance of a praise opener
chart_title: Seed {seed}: how much rarer praise gets with cue B on
foot: Source: Qwen3-8B, last 2 of 36 layers trained by reward (LoRA); 5 seeds per group; checked every 8 updates on 64 held-out prompts; Nov 2026 · athanorscience.com
